solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post, which drops the counts, so each count is read off the blogger's answer

clue.text: Enemy banks on hidden blast

parts.note: a foe is an enemy

indicators.note: the banks of a river are its two edges, so only the outside letters of the next word are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of hidden

explanation.surface: Soldiers fear the foe is massing on the riverbanks, ready to unleash a concealed explosion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hidden' looks like it signals a concealed word, but it is only the source of two edge letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A foehn is a warm dry wind blowing down Alpine slopes, and a blast is a strong gust of wind.

clue.text: Loyal group is cool with Billy (7, two words)

parts.note: to fan is to cool with moving air
a billy, or billy club, is a policeman's truncheon

explanation.surface: A devoted circle of supporters is relaxed about someone called Billy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Billy' looks like a name; it is a truncheon.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan club is an organised body of devoted admirers of a celebrity or team.

clue.text: Across the military board nothing cultivates the lot captured (9, three words)

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: something captured is held inside, so one word is enclosed by the other

parts.note: to farm land is to cultivate it
the lot means all of it

explanation.surface: An army report: nothing is grown on the base, and every item has been seized.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'of all arms' describes something spanning every branch of the armed forces, hence across the military.

clue.text: Such as Mnemosyne's daughters, name each in odd piece

indicators.note: in places the preceding letters within the following word

parts.note: an odd end is a leftover scrap, as in odds and ends
N is the abbreviation for name
EA is the abbreviation for each

explanation.surface: An instruction to list each of the goddess's daughters by name in an unusual work.
explanation.walkthrough: Mnemosyne, goddess of memory, bore Zeus nine daughters, the Muses.
explanation.definitionFit: An ennead is a group of nine, and the Muses formed exactly such a set of nine sisters.

clue.text: Middle England dispensed with lightweight

indicators.note: something dispensed with is done without, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: a no-one is a nobody, a person of no importance
E is the abbreviation for England

explanation.surface: Middle England has rejected a politician of little substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle England' reads as one phrase, the conservative middle class, but the two words split into definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Noon is the middle of the day, midday.

clue.text: Who thumbs that woman taking up passion?

indicators.note: to take something up is to take it on board, so one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: pronoun for that woman
an itch is a strong desire or passion

explanation.surface: A question about who idly twiddles their thumbs while some woman throws herself into a new passion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thumbs' looks like idle twiddling, but it means thumbing a lift.
explanation.definitionFit: A hitchhiker travels by holding out a thumb to passing drivers, so a hitcher is one who thumbs rides.

clue.text: Hearts are on brand in plant

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games
taken as written
to sear is to burn a mark, as with a brand

explanation.surface: Lovers' hearts are branded onto a tree or shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: Hare's-ear is the name of several plants, notably an umbellifer of the genus Bupleurum.

clue.text: First of two children could give you a shock

indicators.note: first of says only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the opening letter of two
a hatch is a brood of young produced together

explanation.surface: Having your first two children can come as quite a jolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' suggests surprise, but it means a thick mass of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A shock of hair is a thick untidy mop, and thatch is informal for a thick head of hair.

clue.text: Rustic Don escapes diet being a wild dancer of old

parts.note: Corydon, the shepherd of pastoral poetry, a stock name for a rustic, minus Don

indicators.note: when something escapes it gets out and is gone, so those letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written; these letters are removed
to bant is to diet, after William Banting's slimming regime

explanation.surface: A country fellow called Don breaks his diet and dances like a wild ancient reveller.
explanation.walkthrough: The rustic is Corydon, a shepherd in Virgil's Eclogues and a stock name for a countryman.
explanation.definitionFit: The Corybantes were priests of Cybele in ancient Phrygia who worshipped with frenzied dancing.

clue.text: About to abandon once rustic project

indicators.note: abandon means leave behind, so that letter drops out of the word

parts.note: a churl was formerly a peasant or countryman
C is circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A countryside scheme of former days is about to be dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'project' looks like a noun, a scheme, but it is the verb to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: To project is to throw forward, the same as to hurl something.

clue.text: Redolent of old caretaker discharging power when upset

indicators.note: upset means turned over, and in a down clue that flips the letters
discharging means letting go, so one letter is released from the word

parts.note: a porter looks after a building
P is the symbol for power

explanation.surface: A building's janitor, fired for losing his temper, reminds people of the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Retro describes a style imitating or evoking an earlier era, so it smells of the past.

clue.text: New hoard found beside river pub

indicators.note: something made new is remade, so these letters are formed into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: the letters of hoard rearranged
the Ouse is an English river, a crossword staple

explanation.surface: A fresh treasure trove has been discovered next to a riverside tavern.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadhouse is an inn or pub standing on a main road outside a town, catering to travellers.

clue.text: Bread, a loaf

parts.note: nan is a flat leavened bread from South Asia
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shopping list item: some bread, specifically a single loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loaf' seems to repeat 'Bread', but it is slang for the head, as in 'use your loaf'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nana is slang, chiefly Australian, for the head, just as loaf is British slang for the head.

clue.text: Echo standard piffle

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
rot is nonsense, piffle

explanation.surface: A complaint that repeating the usual talk is just nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to repeat words mechanically, which is what echoing someone means.

clue.text: Virtually disengaged retreat is most perfect

indicators.note: virtually means almost but not quite, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: clear (disengaged, free) without its last letter
a nest is a snug retreat

explanation.surface: A near-total withdrawal from the world is the ideal hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: To clear out of something is to get disengaged from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleanest in the sense of most flawless or unblemished, the purest and most perfect state.

clue.text: Indecent and very Irish form of writing (9, two words)

parts.note: free in the sense of improper or too forward
V is the abbreviation for very
Erse is the Gaelic language of Ireland

explanation.surface: Something exceptionally rude and Irish, like a bawdy limerick.
explanation.definitionFit: Free verse is poetry without regular metre or rhyme, a form of literary writing.

clue.text: No longer together, everyone returned pack animals

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so these letters are read from the end

parts.note: sam is an obsolete Spenserian word for together
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Once parted, the whole group came back home with their beasts of burden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer' marks an obsolete word, a Chambers-only sense found in Mephisto puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: Llamas are South American camelids kept as beasts of burden, carrying loads in mountain country.

clue.text: Muscle shown by rushing steamers

indicators.note: things rushing about are thrown into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Speeding steamships display brute strength.
explanation.definitionFit: The masseter is the jaw muscle that raises the lower jaw in chewing.

clue.text: Write off a fighter

parts.note: to scrap something is to write it off
per means a, as in so much a head

explanation.surface: An instruction to cancel a combatant's contract.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrapper is someone who loves a scrap, a fight, so a combative person.

clue.text: Writer's book I take round

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for book
taken as written
R is recipe, Latin for take, on prescriptions
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: An author talks of carrying their own book around with them.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A Biro is a ballpoint pen, so it is literally a thing that writes.

clue.text: Sauce got hot inside close to grill

indicators.note: inside says one item is placed within the other word

parts.note: to get angry is to become angry, so got can mean became
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of grill

explanation.surface: A dish heated up when placed near the grill.
explanation.definitionFit: Béchamel is the classic French white sauce made of milk thickened with a butter and flour roux.

clue.text: East-west indicators in desert causing concern for pilots (7, two words)

indicators.note: in sets the pair of letters within the following word

parts.note: to desert is to leave
E and W, the compass points marked on a weathervane

explanation.surface: Signs pointing across a desert worry aviators flying overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: A lee wave is a standing atmospheric wave downwind of a mountain, creating turbulence that pilots must watch for.

clue.text: Right fool donning Celtic poet's armour

indicators.note: to don clothing is to put it on, so the poet wraps around the other pieces like a garment

parts.note: a bard is a poet, especially in the Celtic tradition
R is the abbreviation for right
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A foolish bard is dressed up in a suit of armour.
explanation.definitionFit: A brassard is a piece of plate armour covering the upper arm.

clue.text: Byzantine censer is separate

indicators.note: Byzantine means intricate and convoluted, so the letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An Orthodox incense burner stands apart from the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To secern is to discriminate or distinguish, keeping things apart, and also to secrete.

clue.text: What got Pericles going? Uninhibited freebootery

parts.note: the Greek letter for Pericles' initial, since he was Greek
racy means risqué, uninhibited

explanation.surface: A question about what started an Athenian statesman's career, answered with lawless plundering.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letter of Pericles is written as the Greek letter pi, since the statesman's name in Greek begins with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Freebooters are pirates, so freebootery is plundering at sea, piracy by another name.

clue.text: Finally ignored farce following first from All Souls for French

indicators.note: ignoring the final part of a word means its last letter is dropped
first from says only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the first letter of All
mess (a farce, a shambles) without its last letter

explanation.surface: An Oxford college farce, staged in French, is snubbed at its ending.
explanation.walkthrough: All Souls is an Oxford college, which makes 'Souls' look like part of a name rather than the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Âmes is the French plural of âme, meaning soul or spirit.

clue.text: Cashier turning a blind eye to second to last in yearbook

indicators.note: turning a blind eye to something means ignoring it, so that letter is left out

parts.note: an annual is a yearbook
the penultimate letter of the word for yearbook

explanation.surface: A bank teller ignores an entry in an annual report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cashier' looks like a bank clerk, but it is the verb to dismiss or void.
explanation.definitionFit: To cashier is to dismiss or discard, and to annul is to cancel or make void.

clue.text: One of the options for a busy

definitions.text: One of the options for a
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the letter a is a recognised abbreviation for several words, and this is one of them

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a menu choice for someone busy; in fact the first part asks for one of the words the abbreviation a can stand for.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers lists a as an abbreviation for active (voice), and an active person is busy and lively.

clue.text: A comic pilot lifted nothing

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting raises the bottom to the top, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: taken as written
Dan Dare is the comic-strip pilot of the Eagle

explanation.surface: A cartoon aviator stole nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Dan Dare was the space pilot hero of the British comic Eagle.
explanation.definitionFit: Nada is Spanish for nothing, used informally in English too.

clue.text: This connects room mostly over lower deck, eg (8, two words)

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so the word loses its final letter
in a down-style flip, over says the shortened word is turned back to front

parts.note: space (room) without its last letter
the lower deck is the ratings of a ship, an example of crew

explanation.surface: A description of a ship's layout, with a cabin largely sitting above the lower deck.
explanation.definitionFit: A cap screw is a threaded fastener with a head, used to join machine parts together.

clue.text: Love being wrapped in soft flannel

indicators.note: being wrapped in means being enclosed, so one letter goes inside the other pair

parts.note: a sap is a soft, gullible person
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A lover is swaddled in a soft flannel cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flannel' looks like a washcloth, which fits the bathroom picture, but it means smooth talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Flannel is British slang for flattery or evasive talk, and soft soap is the same kind of flattery.

clue.text: Better put Golden Delicious, or similar, on Newton

indicators.note: in an across clue, placing one thing on another sets it after, so the first-named piece goes second

parts.note: N is the symbol for the newton, the unit of force
an eater is an apple for eating raw, as opposed to a cooker

explanation.surface: A suggestion to drop a nice apple on Isaac Newton, recalling his famous falling-apple story.
explanation.walkthrough: Golden Delicious is a dessert apple; British greengrocers call such apples eaters.
explanation.definitionFit: Neater means tidier or more skilful, an improvement in quality, so better in that comparative sense.

clue.text: A discussion about change seen in Istanbul

indicators.note: about suggests turning around, so the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a rap is a talk or discussion

explanation.surface: A conversation about money changing hands in a Turkish city.
explanation.definitionFit: The para was a small Turkish coin, a fraction of the piastre, so loose coins in Istanbul.

clue.text: Rude wean snapping back of kimmer's knickers, say

indicators.note: snapping means breaking, so the letters are broken up and set in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so only its final letter is used

parts.note: the final letter of kimmer

explanation.surface: A cheeky Scottish child snaps the waistband of a woman's knickers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snapping' reads as twanging elastic but signals the letters breaking apart; wean is Scots for a child, and a kimmer is a Scots gossip or woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Knickers are one example of underwear, hence 'say' marking the definition by example.

clue.text: Pupil left with somebody who's salaried

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
an earner is someone paid a salary

explanation.surface: A student has gone off with a paid worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A learner is someone being taught, the basic sense of a pupil or student.

clue.text: One who'll benefit from exercises — Rab C's always included

indicators.note: something included is taken within, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercises at school
aye is Scots for always, and Rab C Nesbitt is a Glaswegian TV character

explanation.surface: A Glaswegian television character insists workouts always do somebody good.
explanation.walkthrough: Rab C Nesbitt is a Scottish sitcom character, so his word is a Scots one.
explanation.definitionFit: A payee is the person to whom money is paid, so the recipient who gains from a payment.
